title: Cluster Steward Mini-Dashboard — Burst Composer & Health Sparklines
creator: Samir Gupta
description:
Problem: Operators need an ultra-compact console surface that gives quick situational awareness and lightweight controls for Dedicated GPU clusters without having to open the full Fleet dashboard. Current dashboards are too wide for in-context operator flows (alerts, incident triage, cost checks).

Scope: Deliver a 'mini-dashboard' tile and detailed flyout that fits into the Reserve Overview and Operator quickpanels. Key features: concise health sparklines (GPU util, kv-cache hit, tail-p90 latency), an editable "Burst Composer" (preset + slider) to configure short bursts of capacity, a simplified autoscale hysteresis toggle, and an instant cost-delta preview.

Constraints: Must be visually compact (tile target 480x260), accessible (WCAG AA), and performant (avoid heavy SVG animations on initial load). Interactions should be reversible and show impact before commit. Engineering needs UA-friendly CSS classes and tokenized spacing to slot into the existing console grid.

Goals:
- Surface 3 high-value metrics with trend + last-minute spike indicators.
- Provide a one-click 'Scale Now' and 'Schedule Burst' flow with quick confirmation and rollback.
- Make autoscale adjustments understandable by non-operators with clear cost delta preview.
- Ensure the mini-dashboard supports multi-cluster and cross-region quick switching.
design_notes: Tile baseline: 480x260 with 8px grid; compact typography (12/14px).
Health sparklines: micro-sparkline + dot for last sample; red/amber/green thresholds map to SLO bands (p50,p90,p99).
Burst Composer: presets (short, medium, long) + slider that controls 'burst quantum' (num GPUs) and 'burst budget' (minutes).
Cost preview: inline, computed estimate for 1h and for the scheduled window using current rate card; show delta and % of hourly spend.
Autoscale UI: two-state toggle (Adaptive / Fixed) with small hysteresis input (5/15/30s) and a 'suggested' policy generated from recent qps histogram (backend).
Accessibility: keyboard focus trap inside flyout, high-contrast indicator for SLO breach, and aria-live for async status updates.
Animations: prefer CSS transitions for sparkline hover; avoid continuous JS-driven animation for battery reasons on on-prem consoles.
acceptance_criteria: Mini-dashboard tile implemented with 3 trend metrics and last-sample badges; matches visual spec in Figma.
Burst Composer supports presets and slider, persists draft on flyout close, and emits an SDK call schema matching ENG contract.
Cost preview accurate to within ±5% using current rate card; shows before user commits burst/scale action.
Autoscale toggle exposes hysteresis control and calls the autoscale API; engineers can map UI inputs to autoscaler config fields.
Accessibility checklist verified and documented; keyboard and screen reader flows pass internal audit.
Unit and visual tests added for key states: SLO breach, burst scheduled, autoscale paused, regional fallback.

2026-03-01 — Diego Martinez (PM): Prioritization note — customers asked for quick 'scale now' during incidents; make that action reachable in <=2 clicks from alert card. Also called out need for audit log entries for scheduled bursts (security).

2026-03-03 — Design critique (all hands): Team preferred 'sparkline-first' variant for mental model alignment with Ops. Action: refine burst presets to map to common SLO-driven profiles (restore, absorb, surge).

2026-03-05 — Nina Patel: Usability test with two operators (internal): they liked the slider for burst quantum but were confused by 'burst budget' unit (minutes vs. percent). Decision: change label to 'Duration (min)' and add an inline tooltip linking to docs.

2026-03-07 — Marcel Chen (Eng): Technical review: confirmed backend supports 'immediate_scale' and 'scheduled_burst' endpoints; warned that computing cost delta for long windows needs a rate-card cache. Eng tasks added: ENG-6421 (rate-card cache) and ENG-6599 (autoscale API surface).

2026-03-09 — Diego Martinez (PM) and Security: requested audit-log flag on scheduled bursts and RBAC check for 'Scale Now' action. Added security_review_required = false for design (engineering will flag if needed).

2026-03-10 — Nina Patel: Hand-off notes posted: final screens in Figma, component list, interaction specs and token mapping. Handoff checklist included: figma link, export tokens, acceptance criteria, and e2e test scenarios. Engineering kickoff meeting set for 2026-03-12.
